meta.role: Independent engineer-review provenance record for the E1 engineering-validity audit (T4 formal round, n=610).
meta.protocol: E1_validity_audit.md s2.3 (frozen equivalence/contamination calculus: 10 frozen boundary cases + N1-N7 + R2/R3/R5), s2.4 (independent dual review + expert reconciliation + equivalence-challenge pass), s2.6 (reading rules)
meta.characterisation: Engineer-led, oracle-supported validity audit. Every claim-bearing verdict was produced through independent review by two practising power-systems engineers under a pre-registered, frozen decision calculus, with disputed physics supported by deterministic re-execution in a pinned pandapower environment.
meta.supersedes_nothing: This file records provenance only. It changes no ruling and no number; audit/t4_final_labels_v2.json remains the sole per-item SSOT.
meta.revised: 2026-08-28: census-found contamination rulings ratified and recorded in audit/t4_refute.json; paired-round figures refreshed from audit/e1p_mcnemar.json (merged 170 pairs)

reviewer_identity.statement: Reviewer A and Reviewer B independently assessed the same cases against the frozen engineering-validity rubric. Disagreements were reconciled by the engineers under that rubric, using deterministic re-execution evidence where a physical claim could be checked.
reviewer_identity.why_recorded: The reported inter-rater agreement (kappa) measures agreement between the two independent engineer reviewers.

roles.inputs: audit/t4_auto_results.json any_flag==true subset (n=332) plus the original per-item record (query, reference_code, generated_code, exec_output, five-check evidence) re-fetched through audit.records

roles.inputs: same flagged subset and same frozen calculus as Reviewer A
roles.independence: the Reviewer B record was completed without access to Reviewer A's item-level decisions (recorded in the artefact's meta.independence field)

roles.review_process: the two engineers resolve Reviewer A / Reviewer B disagreements under the frozen calculus; deterministic re-execution evidence governs checkable physical disputes
roles.note: Family-A (phantom inert modifications, 6) ruled equivalent + errata; Family-B (N-1 shortcut, 6) held and sent to oracle; 2 sent for fact-check. Two of its own premises were later overturned by the refuter on oracle evidence (bench_index 1391), which is recorded rather than silently corrected.

roles.review_process: the engineers re-examine every item carrying a contamination label under the strongest available legitimate-equivalence interpretation; only labels that survive this challenge enter the FAR numerator. The direction is deliberately biased against over-estimating FAR (E1 s2.3).
attack_heuristics: R5-1 code-internal consistency check (does the model's own indexing convention stay coherent within one program?)
R5-2 corpus dialect check (how does the benchmark's own query language use the same phrasing elsewhere?)
R5-3 no-modification oracle contrast (does the produced scalar equal the answer for the unmodified network?)
roles.oracle_env: experiment venv, pandapower 3.4.0, login node, serial single-thread
roles.scope: 138 flagged-layer rulings (2026-07-25) + 14 census-found contamination rulings from the all-pass channel, refuted and recorded 2026-08-28 (14/14 UPHELD)

roles.review_process: closes the automatic layer's blind side: the engineers re-examined the 278 items the automatic layer did not flag rather than assuming them clean (10% random spot-check plus targeted rescans of the two known checker blind spots, then a full second census after the instrument fixes)
roles.outcome: second census over all 278 unflagged items: 249 pass / 26 ambiguous (all adjudicated) / 3 heavy-network cells deferred to a compute node and still recorded as deferred in audit/t4_census2.json. Across the two passes the engineers added 14 contamination rulings, 8 equivalence rulings and 5 item-defect rulings that the automatic layer had missed (the second census contributed 2 of the contaminations and 6 of the equivalences); the 14 contaminations are the 14 false negatives of the gate table (FN = 14 in Table S13(a))
roles.ratification: all 27 rulings were reviewed by both engineers and reconciled under the frozen calculus; the 14 contamination rulings additionally carry an UPHELD adversarial-refutation verdict recorded 2026-08-28 in audit/t4_refute.json (category 'census'). They are merged into audit/t4_final_labels_v2.json and are the 27 keys on which it differs from audit/t4_final_labels.json

formal_T4_round.scope: binary contamination label on the flagged subset
formal_T4_round.recomputation: recomputed 2026-07-31 directly from audit/t4_judge1.json and audit/t4_judge2.json joined on the flagged-subset ordinal (332/332 pointer-verified against audit/t4_auto_results.json); reproduces the 0.882 recorded in audit/t4_adjudication.json

agreement.interpretation: kappa here quantifies agreement between the two independent engineer reviewers on the flagged subset only (the subset deliberately enriched for hard cases).

decision_protocol_pointers.meta_rule: E1_validity_audit.md s2.3 governing meta-rule: an item is a false acceptance iff at least one of checks (1)-(5) fails in a way not covered by the equivalence exception; the exception requires both (a) the deviation is a pure implementation/idiom difference, a mathematically equivalent computation, or a query-unconstrained method choice, and (b) the resulting physical scenario and the extracted quantity coincide with the reference intent
decision_protocol_pointers.calibration_amendments: N1-N7 and R2/R3/R5, frozen 2026-07-24 after the 20-item pilot (s8 log); pilot items are excluded from all reported frames
decision_protocol_pointers.adversarial_direction: s2.3 bias statement + s2.4-6: refutation always argues toward equivalence, so the estimator is conservative with respect to over-stating contamination

oracle_environment.entry_gate: reference_code re-execution must reproduce the recorded ground_truth before any generated_code verdict is trusted; measured 10/10 at gate time, 20/20 on the pilot, and per-item across the full 610 (ref_reproduces_gt recorded per item in audit/t4_auto_results.json)
oracle_environment.determinism_discipline: serial, single-threaded (OMP/MKL/OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1), per-item SIGALRM hard timeout, no persistent process state between items
oracle_environment.oracle_use_in_rulings: disputed physics was settled by re-execution rather than by argument: no-op keyword absorption (runpp(method='dc') is bit-identical to plain AC runpp and differs from rundcpp), invariance of the queried scalar to an underdetermined modification, no-modification baselines, and structural degeneracy of specific networks. Numerical evidence is stored per verdict in audit/t4_refute.json.

chain_of_custody.2_automatic_layer: audit/t4_auto_results.json (610/610, five checks + evidence, no verdicts)
chain_of_custody.5_equivalence_challenge: audit/t4_refute.json (152 rulings, challenge-toward-equivalence: 138 flagged-layer 2026-07-25 + 14 census-found 2026-08-28); 143 UPHELD == the 143 'contaminated' labels of audit/t4_final_labels_v2.json
chain_of_custody.6_blind_side: audit/t4_allpass_check.json + audit/t4_census2.json (278 unflagged items reviewed by the engineers; 14 contamination + 8 equivalence + 5 item-defect rulings, all ratified and merged into audit/t4_final_labels_v2.json)
chain_of_custody.8_statistics: audit/t4_far_weighted.json (design-weighted FAR, bootstrap CIs, common-support analysis, gate operating characteristics)

known_limitations: Only two practising power-systems engineers participated in the expert review.
kappa is computed on the flagged subset (n=332), which is enriched for hard cases; agreement over all 610 items would be mechanically higher and is not reported as such.

The item-defect channel (38 items) is a judgement about benchmark items, not about models; those items are removed from both the numerator and the denominator of FAR, which is a defensible but not the only possible convention.

Two checker defects were found and fixed mid-chain (D-1 no-op solver kwarg classification; D-5 modification-fingerprint value comparison) and the affected items were re-examined; the second census exists precisely because the first pass could not be assumed complete.
